context: A uni student interviews a retired diplomat at home
purpose: Teach: 終戦/祝福/ノルウェー/義務教育/にまつわる/極東/篇/携わっ

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 本日はお時間をいただき、ありがとうございます。卒論で、終戦直後の日本外交にまつわるテーマを扱っておりまして。
lines.en: Thank you for your time today. My thesis deals with topics related to Japan's diplomacy right after the war ended.
lines.style: Polite, slightly nervous student opening an interview with measured formality.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: いやいや、こんな老いぼれを訪ねてくれて、こちらこそ祝福したいくらいだよ。さあ、座って座って。
lines.en: No no, I should be the one congratulating you for visiting an old man like me. Come, sit down.
lines.style: Warm, self-deprecating elder voice with gentle welcoming cadence.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 恐れ入ります。早速ですが、先生は若い頃、北欧、特にノルウェー大使館に赴任されたと伺いました。
lines.en: I'm honored. So to begin, I heard that in your younger years you were posted to Northern Europe, particularly the Norwegian embassy.
lines.style: Crisp respectful student tone moving the interview forward carefully.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ああ、ノルウェーね。記憶を辿ると、もう五十年も前か。私が義務教育を受けていた頃は、外国なんて月より遠く感じたものだ。
lines.en: Ah, Norway. Tracing my memory, that was already fifty years ago. Back when I was in compulsory schooling, foreign countries felt farther than the moon.
lines.style: Reflective elder reminiscing with slow nostalgic pacing and dry humor.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: なるほど。その後、極東の安全保障に長く携わってこられたんですよね。
lines.en: I see. And after that, you were involved for a long time in Far East security affairs, correct?
lines.style: Attentive student steering the conversation back to substantive matters.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: そうだね。私の回顧録の後篇は、ほぼその仕事の話で埋まっている。地味だが、誰かがやらねばならん仕事だった。
lines.en: That's right. The later volume of my memoir is filled almost entirely with that work. Unglamorous, but someone had to do it.
lines.style: Modest elder statesman tone, understated pride beneath plain delivery.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: ぜひ後篇も拝読したいです。最後に、これから外交に携わっていく学生に、一言いただけますか。
lines.en: I would love to read that later volume too. Finally, could you give a word to students who will work in diplomacy from now on?
lines.style: Earnest closing question delivered with sincere admiration.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 焦らず、現場を見ること。本に書いてないことの方が多いからね。君の歩む道に祝福があらんことを。
lines.en: Don't rush; see the field with your own eyes. There's more not written in books than what is. May blessings follow your path.
lines.style: Grandfatherly closing benediction, warm and quietly authoritative.
